title: feat(storage): recover validated PNG images to reviewed new ZIPs
body:
## Why

Advance Stage 6 of the storage roadmap with recovery of complete supported PNG images from a bounded damaged file or image. The implementation, source reconciliations and qualification state are preserved as incremental remote checkpoints.

## Resulting behavior

- **Recover PNG images to ZIP…** is available for one native local regular file of at most 64 MiB, through the context menu, Tools menu and command palette.
- The scan reviews candidate source ranges, dimensions and findings. Only validated noninterlaced 8-bit grayscale/RGB/gray-alpha/RGBA PNGs are selectable. CRCs, chunk ordering, complete zlib framing/Adler, exact scanline lengths and filter bytes must pass.
- Selected PNGs and `recovery-report.json` are written to a separately verified new ZIP. The report retains source offsets, hashes, classifications and coverage; no original filesystem names are claimed.
- The shared queue owns admitted work. Publication rehashes source and staged output after the durable committing checkpoint. A new native exclusive-publication guard checks captured authority/cancellation synchronously after the final asynchronous path probe; pause epochs force fresh proofs, including a transient pause/resume.
- Existing destinations and source files are retained. A completed install remains successful if Stop or a completion observer arrives afterward. Restart requires a fresh scan and review; the journal retains digests/receipts, not source bytes.
- No runtime dependency was added. New code is original MIT; the existing source inventory records SHA-256 integrity use without changing encryption or distribution decisions.

## Reconciliation

Current saved checkpoint: **dd77efcb570bf1344d2cfca32a7f590abe6349dc**. The latest combined application-source checkpoint is **6ce4d522bc1e7283f0839a98f4efab4461454bcd**.

The resumed integration includes main through `ab7f1536` (merged PR #117), PR #116 at `bda0374b`, the worksheet/document-workspace work, and the separate local-qualification branch through `8a4cc8b6`. Incoming evidence is retained unchanged with its original source scope. Superseded branch heads were audited for unique work.

The current application mirrors canonical Quds **0ca0d31bd757da4db6b6ef45764ff9de33990a2f** and standalone parser **d422fa99a3a84830794f0e2dc332d59f923779f7**. This combines bounded, namespace-aware ODS import, grouped rows and inherited styles with blank-row, covered-cell and quoted-formula preservation fixes. The final observed canonical update, `ddaca09c` (09:37:28 UTC cutoff), is being reconciled for default styles and time formats before the final source freeze.

## Validation status

**The previous disk-capacity blocker is resolved. Fresh local qualification is in progress; this PR remains a draft.**

The workspace now has the pinned Flutter 3.47.8 / Dart 3.13.7 toolchain, locked dependencies and genuine native compilers. Native application libraries compile successfully without disabling hooks or substituting libraries. The final planned cohorts are 49 application suites, seven editor suites and 17 engine suites.

Completed development checks include 32 application document-service tests, 35 canonical ODS tests at `0ca0d31b`, and 36 focused date/time-format tests on the pending canonical reconciliation. Strict focused analysis also passes for those formatter files. The previously saved 52-file app analysis gate passed before the later source reconciliation. These development/predecessor results are not presented as final acceptance for the forthcoming combined source.

The first source audit verified 10,429 checkout files and all 2,223 managed Office files, including SHA-256, canonical Git blobs and modes. Its aggregate failed because the scripted oracle was attempted before engine output generation; all failure evidence remains intact. The final source-only controls and output-dependent oracle now have separate scheduled gates.

Each final gate will bind the saved source commit and before/after source and resolution hashes, retain raw output and strict machine counts, and be committed remotely immediately, including failures. The remaining gates cover focused strict analysis; app/editor/engine suites; source integrity; engine-produced DOCX/XLSX/PPTX oracle checks; PNG recovery on Dart VM and actual compiled JavaScript with independent Python readers; and separate font-backed navigation captures.

All incremental checkpoints use `[skip ci]`. **No GitHub Actions run has been awaited or restarted.**

[Current continuation and evidence](https://github.com/CrispStrobe/CrispCloud/tree/dd77efcb570bf1344d2cfca32a7f590abe6349dc/docs/evidence/storage-carving-20261115/local-resume-20261115T1010) · [Profile and limits](https://github.com/CrispStrobe/CrispCloud/blob/dd77efcb570bf1344d2cfca32a7f590abe6349dc/docs/archive-png-carving.md)

## Boundaries

64 MiB input/output and separate bounded parser-work/expansion limits. Indexed/interlaced/animated PNGs, other bit depths, unknown/compressed ancillary chunks and smaller zlib windows explicitly decline. Fragment reconstruction, original names/directories, physical devices, rescue imaging, undelete and JPEG/PDF carving remain future profiles.

Portable core acceptance does not enable browser/cloud publication or establish other-platform execution. The native verify/rename boundary is not atomic compare-and-swap against arbitrary external writers. This is a draft implementation review, not a signed release or broad Office rendering/schema acceptance.
